title: Region-prioritized analytics fanout with privacy zones and evacuation channels
creator: Asha Khanna
description: Goal: implement a region-prioritized fanout layer for console usage telemetry that enforces customer privacy zones, provides graceful evacuation channels when regional capacity or policy blocks writes, and produces strong observability for residency decisions. This ticket scopes the backend service changes, pipeline gating rules, and a gradual rollout plan to avoid reprocessing storms.
acceptance_criteria: Console telemetry requests include a tenant_region header and are routed to a primary storage region if tenant has a residency policy
Requests rejected by primary due to legal hold or capacity produce a deterministic evacuation path and are queued to a fallback region with audit metadata
Analytics replication metadata and decisions are emitted to the residency-audit topic and surfaced in the Console SLO dashboard
No duplicate events created during evacuation (at-least-once ingestion prevented by idempotent write keys and dedupe window)
End-to-end performance impact on median write latency <= 15ms and p95 <= 120ms for normal traffic profile
Feature gated and rolloutable: can be toggled per-org and per-route, with metrics enabling automated rollback
implementation_steps: Design: finalize fanout routing table format (region_priority list, legal_flags, fallback_tiers) and residency decision API (sync + async hooks)
Backend: extend console-ingest service to evaluate tenant residency policy at request time and attach routing metadata
Queueing: add evacuation queue support in ingestion cluster; implement per-tenant idempotency key derivation for dedupe
Replication: update analytics-ingest workers to honor evacuation metadata and write audit tuples to residency-audit topic
Observability: add tracing tags for route_decision, evacuation_reason, fallback_region; dashboard panels for evacuated_write_rate and dedupe_hits
Policy: implement a light-weight legal_hold check backed by policy-service cache with TTL 30s
Testing: run chaos tests to simulate primary region rejection, capacity exhaustion, and legal hold toggles
Documentation: write Console operations playbook and sample queries for SRE and Account teams
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature flag in non-prod and run synthetic traffic for 48h. 2) Canary 1% of production orgs in us-east with detailed tracing and dedupe monitoring. 3) Expand to 10% and verify evacuated_write_rate and no duplicate counts. 4) Gradual expansion by region, with manual hold for EU until KMS integration completes. 5) Full enable once SLA and audit logs are validated.
migration_plan: For existing tenants with no residency policy, default behavior remains multi-region mirror. For tenants with residency constraints, a one-time backfill job will reconcile historical analytics to primary region retention buckets; backfill is opt-in and rate-limited to avoid pipeline saturation.
test_plan: Unit tests for routing table evaluation and fallback selection
Integration test: simulate primary write rejection and assert evacuation metadata flows to residency-audit topic
End-to-end canary: validate dedupe by injecting same event id across primary and fallback and assert single downstream record
Load test: 2x expected peak with evacuation mode enabled to validate queue retention and throughput
Compliance test: toggle legal_hold flag and ensure writes are blocked and audit entries are produced
notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous policy checks add <10ms median; we use cached policy-service to avoid per-request DB hits. Asynchronous retries improve throughput but complicate deterministic auditing.
Open question: whether fallback writes should be encrypted with tenant-specific keys in fallback region; blocked pending KMS cross-region support decision (see RFC #ENG-RFC-2026-11)
Related infra ticket: ENG-63218 (regional-write-affinity-evacuation-playbook) has operational runbooks to reuse
Proposed dedupe window is 5 minutes; longer windows increase memory for idempotency store but reduce duplication risk during large cross-region replays
